title: Loop iter 2: larger-n Sonnet pass to tighten the rank-ceiling CIs (#342)
design: SAME light blinded clickability elicitation as iter1, on a FRESH DISJOINT slice of 150 representable cases (canonical baseline=variant0 pairing), to reach credible-n (SMR gate 100, MCC gate 150) and tighten CIs
scoring: directional_gate G0-G11, delta=0.0, budget=37 (top 25%), bootstrap=2000 over experiments, 90% CIs, seed=42

hypotheses.H1: sonnet_panel balanced SMR holds >= 0.62 with Wilson 90% LB > 0.55 at n=150 (above chance, tight)
hypotheses.H2: sonnet_panel MCC 90% LB stays > 0 at n=150
hypotheses.H3: does sonnet_panel now CLEAR any GO gate? predicted: G5(MCC) maybe; G4(SMR>=0.70) NO; overall verdict NO-GO (sub-decision-grade)

decision_rule: If SMR holds >=0.62 (LB>0.55) and MCC LB>0 at n=150 -> firm 'above-chance but sub-decision-grade' result for the whitepaper; heavy $275 pass only justified if testing the heavy-architecture hypothesis specifically (needs user consent). If signal collapses to chance -> iter1 was n=60 noise; ceiling is model-robust.
